blocks.note: first meaning: the answer to 8 down, a raised bank holding back water
second meaning: the riverside road along the Thames in central London

explanation.walkthrough: 8 down is DYKE, and a dyke is an EMBANKMENT; the Embankment is also the road running beside the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is a raised earth bank, and the Victoria Embankment is a well-known Thames-side thoroughfare in the capital.

clue.text: One letting nothing go has a second difficult problem

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a tickler is a puzzling or tricky matter

explanation.surface: A perfectionist who lets nothing slide faces another knotty problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler insists on exact standards and will not overlook the smallest lapse or detail.

blocks.note: first meaning: belonging to the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad
second meaning: birds bred to fly back to their loft

explanation.surface: A classical poet keeps a flock of pigeons.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first half as HOMER'S, the possessive of the poet; the plural noun is homing pigeons.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer is the ancient Greek bard, and racing pigeons that fly back to their loft are called homers.

clue.text: It is pushed out on the Spree!

definitions.text: It is pushed out on the Spree!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone splashing out lavishly on a spending spree
setter's reading: the Spree is the river through Berlin, where a small craft is launched

explanation.surface: Something lavishly celebrated during a night of extravagance.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'push the boat out' means to spend freely on a spree; here the Spree is literally the Berlin river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small vessel is shoved off from the bank onto a river, here the German waterway named Spree.

blocks.note: surface reading: a builder who laid and lifted a building's base
setter's reading: a charitable institution, for which money was raised

explanation.walkthrough: The image is of bricklaying, but the foundation is a charity and raising means funding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron who gives money to set up or support a charitable institution is its generous donor.

blocks.note: a sapphire is a gem, with the possessive S kept
a shade of colour is a tone

explanation.surface: Describing the colour of a jacinth as resembling a sapphire's.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacinth is an orange variety of zircon, an example of a precious stone; 'possibly' marks the example.

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author has their name printed on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow tapering banner, once carried on a knight's lance.

indicators.note: a king dressed in colour is wrapped inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a dye is a colouring substance
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch painted in vivid colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is OFFA, the Mercian king whose earthwork along the Welsh border is Offa's DYKE.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa of Mercia ordered the long earthen bank on the Welsh border that bears his name.

clue.text: It measures the speed of the wind, etc

definitions.text: It measures the speed of the wind, etc

blocks.note: surface reading: the weather instrument measuring how fast the air blows
setter's reading: the wind section of an orchestra and the other players, kept in tempo

explanation.walkthrough: An anemometer comes to mind first, but 'etc' hints that the wind is a section of musicians, along with strings and brass.
explanation.definitionFit: The ticking device marks a steady tempo, so it sets the pace for players of wind instruments and others.

indicators.note: the clever youngster's possession is something the words themselves hold within them

blocks.note: end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: Every bright child owns something of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean all members of a group taken one at a time, as in each day or every day.

clue.text: Very old description, in part, of some hymns

definitions.text: description, in part, of some hymns

blocks.note: first meaning: dating from the distant past

blocks.clueFragment: description, in part, of some hymns
blocks.note: second meaning: one word from the title of a famous Anglican hymn book

explanation.surface: A dated characterisation of some church hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: Hymns Ancient and Modern is a long-established Church of England hymnal, so the word describes part of its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to antiquity, and it half-describes the hymnal titled Hymns Ancient and Modern.

blocks.note: first meaning: the French word for petrol
second meaning: a concentrated aromatic extract from a plant

explanation.surface: Vehicles in France run on a particular kind of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: In French, essence is petrol (gasoline), so French motorists fill up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: French drivers buy fuel called by this name, and an aromatic plant extract is an essential oil.

blocks.note: surface reading: the achievements of the Victorian prime minister Robert Peel
setter's reading: John Peel, the Cumbrian huntsman of the folk song, whose triumphs were foxes caught

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel the statesman is the false trail; John Peel of 'D'ye ken John Peel' was a famous fox-hunter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter's successes are the animals brought down, and the carcasses are proof of a good day's hunting.

clue.text: Simple girl nearly rode back on donkey

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the word that follows loses its final letter
going back means the shortened word is read from right to left

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
taken as written
Ned, short for neddy, is a donkey

explanation.surface: A plain young woman almost rode home on a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain and undecorated, with no ornament added, is simple in style.

indicators.note: something wretched is in a sorry, broken state, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grubby, miserable man huddled in an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean and likely to spread germs is a synonym for dirty.

clue.text: Doormats where shadows fall on institutions

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing falling on another means it sits directly above it

blocks.note: to shadow someone is to follow them closely, to dog them
organisations and institutions are bodies

explanation.surface: Mats by the entrance lie where shade falls across official buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are walked over and given menial chores are both drudges and doormats.

clue.text: Shocking! That's their anger out of control

indicators.note: anger out of control runs wild, so the letters fly out of their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An outburst of rage so wild it is genuinely alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so momentous and startling that it seems to shake the world is utterly shocking.

clue.text: Safety device heartlessly shattered in crash

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the following word is dropped
a crash smashes things up, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its middle letter is the fifth of nine

explanation.surface: A safety device ruthlessly smashed to pieces in a collision.
explanation.definitionFit: The padded support on a car seat protects the neck from whiplash in a collision.

clue.text: Rita is at the heart of this nuisance

blocks.clueFragment: Rita is at the heart of this
blocks.note: surface reading: a woman called Rita causing all the trouble
setter's reading: the name's four letters sit as the middle four of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A woman named Rita lies behind all the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: With eight letters, the answer has RITA at its centre, flanked by IR and NT: IR-RITA-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that annoys or vexes, like grit in the eye, is a persistent nuisance.

clue.text: Where Horatio asked for the kiss of death?

definitions.text: Where Horatio asked for the kiss of death?

blocks.note: surface reading: an idiom for something that dooms a venture
setter's reading: Admiral Horatio Nelson's dying words, 'Kiss me, Hardy', to his flag captain

explanation.walkthrough: Horatio is Nelson, who was fatally wounded at sea in 1805 and asked his captain Hardy to kiss him as he died.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1805 naval battle off Cape Trafalgar in Spain was where Nelson died after asking Hardy for a kiss.

clue.text: The most effective notes in case

blocks.note: two musical notes, A and B
lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'

explanation.surface: The most powerful musical notes kept in their case.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of able describes whoever is the most competent and capable.

blocks.note: first meaning: a cordial of fruit juice, sugar and rum or vinegar
second meaning: absinthe is wormwood, a woody plant

explanation.walkthrough: Absinthe looks like the liquor, but it is also the name of wormwood, the bushy plant that flavours it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is an old fruit-and-spirit cordial, and wormwood (absinthe) is a woody bush, an example.

blocks.note: surface reading: overcast skies, a weather report
setter's reading: the word is near the Gloucestershire town's name, differing by a single letter

explanation.surface: A weather forecast of overcast skies around a Cotswold town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stroud is a town in Gloucestershire; change its second letter and you have a word for an enveloping covering of cloud or mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pall of mist or cloud that envelops a hill is described as a shroud.

blocks.note: surface reading: an explosion, or losing one's temper
setter's reading: a photographer making a bigger print

explanation.walkthrough: A 'blow-up' is a photographer's word for a bigger print made from a negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a larger print of a photograph from its negative is called blowing it up.

clue.text: Touchy about a familiar London statue

indicators.note: turned about means the word for touchy is read the other way round

blocks.note: someone sore is touchy and easily upset

explanation.surface: Someone sensitive about a well-known London monument.
explanation.walkthrough: The winged statue at Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: The aluminium winged archer atop the Shaftesbury Memorial in Piccadilly Circus is known everywhere by this name.

clue.text: Trees do provide strength for a Danish physicist

indicators.note: to provide is to make something from given material, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Trees supply power to a scientist from Denmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strength' is apt: the oersted, named after him, is a unit of magnetic field strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Oersted was the Danish scientist who discovered that electric currents create magnetic fields.

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the county name
in a down clue, brought up means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of the county name

explanation.surface: A monarch raised in an English Midlands county.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire lay within Mercia, Offa's kingdom, which makes the surface fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was the eighth-century ruler of Mercia, the Anglo-Saxon kingdom covering the English Midlands.

blocks.note: setter's reading: a group of musicians, here the Manchester rock group
surface reading: a strip of green vegetation, a fertile spot in a desert

explanation.walkthrough: Band means a strip, but it is also a pop group; the Britpop band from Manchester shares its name with a fertile spot in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile watered patch amid desert is a patch of green, and also the name of a 1990s rock group.

blocks.note: surface reading: control or sway held over another person
setter's reading: a drunk is said to be under the sway of alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: Someone drunk is 'under the' answer, so the answer sits over them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway or control over others is this word, and drink driving is legally termed driving under it.
